scope: The delivery stack of India's direct-benefit and distribution schemes, 2013–2026: who takes a margin, a contract or a political dividend between treasury and beneficiary. Covers the DBT rails (NPCI APB, PFMS, banks, BC networks — Fino, CSC SPV, IPPB, Airtel Payments Bank), Ujjwala's OMC channel, PMGKAY's FCI channel, free-bus schemes and their bus OEM awards (Karnataka, Delhi), consumer-goods tenders (UP laptops 2012, TN laptops, Punjab and Rajasthan smartphones), Amma canteens, the paid volunteer layer in Andhra Pradesh, and the publicity layer (state and central advertising spend on leader-branded schemes: Centre, Delhi, Telangana, MP, Maharashtra). Core scheme records for Ladli Behna and Ladki Bahin live in the sibling women-cash file; here they carry only the publicity/delivery layer. Deliberately left out for want of an opened source: Telangana Mahalakshmi bus procurement, Rythu Bandhu/Samagra/Ladki Bahin portal vendors, BJP labharthi outreach and PM letters, cylinder manufacturers, FCI contractors, SBI's DBT share. Every URL listed in sources was opened; search-snippet-only facts are listed in gaps, not in claims.

symmetryCheck: The same three lenses were pointed at governments of six parties. (1) Publicity spend: BJP Centre ₹5,987 crore over 11 years (₹910 crore print FY21–25, largest recipient Times of India); AAP Delhi ₹612.80 crore in 2022 and a CAG finding of SC-guideline breach; BRS Telangana ~₹300 crore 2014–18 by RTI; BJP MP ₹290 crore on one scheme; Mahayuti Maharashtra ₹199.81 crore on one scheme in four months. The lens returns a large figure for every government it is pointed at (5/5), so publicity spend alone is non-discriminating; the discriminating fact is that only Delhi has an audit finding, and only Delhi was audited on the point — a scrutiny asymmetry, not a behaviour asymmetry. (2) Bus procurement: Congress Karnataka and AAP Delhi both award to Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland/Switch and JBM (6 of 7 awards), so OEM concentration reflects market structure, not party favour; Karnataka's fleet actually shrank under Shakti and the state owes its RTCs ₹5,172 crore. (3) Paid last-mile intermediaries: YSRCP's 2.56 lakh volunteers (₹1,536 crore/yr) drew EC action on opposition complaints; the BJP's labharthi outreach could not be documented from an opened source, so the evidence is asymmetric in the other direction and is recorded as speculative, not as exoneration. Consumer-goods schemes split evenly: SP (UP laptops, HP; 8.7 lakh undistributed) and Congress (Punjab, Rajasthan phones) lost the next election; AIADMK (51 lakh laptops) lost in 2021; the DMK revived the scheme 13 months before 2026. The one documented abuse of the DBT rail (Airtel, ₹190 crore, 2017) involved a private payments bank under a BJP government and was reversed by a BJP-government regulator.
